newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end strong, conglomerates lead.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end strong, conglomerates lead.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended on a strong note on Tuesday, with the Hang Seng Index staging an encouraging push above 13,500 points, led by gains in the conglomerate sector.
The Hang Seng index closed 97.36 points, or 0.72 percent, higher at 13,548.43. But turnover was a slow HK$6.74 billion compared with HK$8.43 billion on Monday.
"People are already discounting steady interest rates," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting body is due to meet later on Tuesday and is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged.
Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities, said the market was staging a technical rebound this week after two sluggish weeks.
"Technically, breaking 13,500 is very positive," added one trader.
Conglomerates were strong performers on Tuesday.
Hutchison Whampoa rose HK$1.25 to HK$59.25 and Wharf Holdings advanced HK$0.20 to HK$35.60.

"People are starting to favour the conglomerates," said Tang. "We are quite cautious about the property market in the first quarter and we like the conglomerate sector because they are not so sensitive to interest rate fluctuations."
Property stocks also had a strong session. "The property stocks seemed to have quite a nice rebound today," said Ho.
Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.75 to HK$92.25 and New World Development added HK$1.25 to HK$50.25.
In the banking sector, Bank of East Asia rose HK$0.40 to HK$34.30 following a decline of HK$1.00 on Monday, and HSBC Holdings advanced HK$1.50 to HK$182.00.
Shares in Lai Sun Development rose HK$0.25 to HK$12.30. The company said it plans to issue about US$100 million in bonds convertible into shares of Asia Television Ltd.
